subject: spanish
title: Family Foundations: Mi Familia
welcome_lead: Learn the core family vocabulary you need to describe your relatives in Spanish.
meta_desc: GCSE Spanish foundations adventure on family vocabulary.
final_note: ¡Genial! Now you can introduce all of mi familia.

walkthroughs.body_html: Most family words follow the pattern: masculine ends in -o with el (el hermano, el abuelo), feminine ends in -a with la (la hermana, la abuela). Exception: la madre and el padre.
To say 'my' use mi (singular) or mis (plural): mi hermano, mis hermanos. Tu = your, su = his/her. Example: Mi madre se llama Ana (My mother is called Ana).
Spanish uses the masculine plural for mixed groups: los hermanos can mean 'brothers' OR 'siblings (brothers + sisters)'. Likewise los padres = 'parents', los abuelos = 'grandparents'.

mcqs.q: How do you say 'My sister is embarrassed' in Spanish?
options: Mi hermana tiene vergüenza / está avergonzada.

mcqs.q: In Spain, how do you address a group of friends informally?

options: Could be his/her/your(formal)/their brother - context determines which.

sequence.def: My great-grandparents — three generations above me
My grandparents — two generations above me
My parents — one generation above me
Me — the reference point of the family tree
My children — one generation below me
My grandchildren — two generations below me
